subject: minimized fit function in lavaan... HOW?

messages.author: 373e56ec89625c50
messages.subject: minimized fit function in lavaan... HOW?
parts:
hello there. so i'm migrating from EQS into lavaan and there's something that i haven't been able to quite figure out. when using the regular chi square test of fit, i know that the standard formula to obtain the chi-square value is (N-1)*F_mL where N is my sample size and F_mL is the minimized fit function.
 
i thought that setting the argument 'verbose=TRUE' in my sem( ) function would give me the minimzed F_mL but i does not. nevertheless, lavaan's results do match EQS' perfectly so something else must be going on somewhere.
 
below is the example i'm working with:
 
library(lavaan)
 
S <- matrix(c(1.0988446, 0.68571489, 0.7145704, 0.9088392, 0.37751345,
     0.6857149, 4.48363524, 0.7262221, 0.5211723, 0.09865005,
     0.7145704, 0.72622207, 2.9842987, 0.9322141, 0.46157840,
     0.9088392, 0.52117226, 0.9322141, 2.6040152, 0.58566978,
     0.3775135, 0.09865005, 0.4615784, 0.5856698, 0.92523364), nrow=5, byrow=T)
colnames(S) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")
rownames(S) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")
 
myModel<-'
     D ~ A + B + C
     E ~ D
     '
fitted<-sem(myModel, sample.cov=S, sample.nobs=108, verbose=TRUE, mimic="EQS")
 
summary(fitted)
 
the last entry on my iteration history obtained through verbose=TRUE is 0.0359718716 and my sample size is 108 so, in theory, 0.0359718716 * (108-1) should give me the Minimum Function Test Statistic  7.698 reported in the output, but it doesn't!! i can see from my EQS that if i fit the same model and request the same output its iteration history stops at 0.07194 and, in this case the formula (0.07194)*(108-1) does work and gives the test statistic reported both in lavaan's and EQS' output.
 
if verbose=TRUE isn't giving me what i'm trying to find, how can i request it? where does lavaan keep its minimized fit function that becomes the test statistic?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: minimized fit function in lavaan... HOW?
parts:
On 09/13/2013 11:09 AM, oolve...@gmail.com wrote:

> the last entry on my iteration history obtained through verbose=TRUE is
> 0.0359718716 and my sample size is 108 so, in theory, 0.0359718716 *
> (108-1) should give me the Minimum Function Test Statistic 7.698
> reported in the output, but it doesn't!!

lavaan uses a slighly different fit function which is 0.5 times the
usual one. Therefore, to go from the minimum fit value (F) to the
chi-square, you need to use: 2 * (N-1) * F:

0.0359718716 * (108-1) * 2 = 7.697981

Having explained this, I will change it (if mimic="EQS") so that we get
the same F values in the output as EQS.

Yves.

   F_mL = log(|Sigma|)-log(|S|)+ tr(S*Sigma^(-1))-p  but uses 0.5*FmL?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: minimized fit function in lavaan... HOW?
parts:
On 09/13/2013 11:52 AM, oolve...@gmail.com wrote:

> F_mL = log(|Sigma|)-log(|S|)+ tr(S*Sigma^(-1))-p but uses 0.5*FmL?
> is there any reason as for why?

You can get rid of a lot of '2*' statements when computing the gradient,
making the code slightly more compact.

The 0.5* version is also sometimes used in the literature (see eg
Joreskog 1971).

The reason why it is like this in lavaan is this: at the early stages of
the lavaan's development, I often used the 'technical appendices' of
Mplus (http://www.statmodel.com/download/techappen.pdf) as a guide.
Equation 96 uses the 0.5* form.

In the end, it doesn't matter.

Yves.
